items.quote: Give up your son so we may eat him today, and tomorrow we’ll eat my son.
items.contrast: The first woman’s son is assigned to today, while the quoted woman’s son is assigned to tomorrow.
items.reason: “The other woman” has no fixed perspective: it could mean the woman other than the speaker or the woman other than the quoted proposer, producing either today or tomorrow. Replacing it with “the woman who proposed the plan’s child” would recover the intended answer, tomorrow. The target meaningfully tests ownership and the two-day sequence.

items.quote: the king had put the officer on whose arm he leaned in charge of the gate, and the people trampled him in the gateway
items.contrast: The officer is trampled, whereas the king is only the person who appointed him.
items.reason: The king is a plausible alternative because he is prominent in the sentence, but “him” refers to the officer just placed in charge of the gate. Resolving that pronoun distinguishes the victim from the appointing king.

items.quote: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul with them during the night and brought him as far as Antipatris. The next day they let the cavalry go on with him, while they returned to the barracks.
items.contrast: The soldiers return to the barracks, while the cavalry continue with Paul.
items.reason: The cavalry are plausible because they are the nearest named group, but the sentence contrasts letting the cavalry go on with the soldiers’ own return. Tracking the two groups resolves who continued and who returned.

items.quote: The five men who had spied out the land went inside and took the idol, the ephod and the household gods while the priest and the six hundred armed men stood at the entrance of the gate.
items.contrast: The five spies enter and take the objects, while the priest and six hundred armed men remain at the entrance.
items.reason: The priest and armed men are plausible because they are present at the scene, but the passage explicitly contrasts their position at the entrance with the five spies’ entry and taking of the objects.

items.quote: So his servant ran him through, and he died. When the Israelites saw that Abimelek was dead
items.contrast: The servant performs the killing, while Abimelek is the person killed.
items.reason: The servant is a plausible alternative because he is the subject performing the action, but “him” is its recipient and the following sentence identifies the dead person as Abimelek. The question tests actor versus victim.
